newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen on sidelines during intervention period.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen on sidelines during intervention period.

text.p: The Federal Reserve was expected to stay out of the banking system before its usual intervention period Wednesday morning.

"Prior to Monday's $5.1 billion 10-day system repurchase agreement, we projected a daily add need of $7.0 billion in the current reserve period," said Kathy Bostjancic, money market analyst at UBS Securities.

"Given Monday's operation, which extends to the end of the reserve period, we now estimate a remaining daily add need of $2.0 billion. The Fed likely will stay on the sidelines today and wait to execute a four-day system repo (Thursday)," Bostjancic said.
Expectations of no action were shared by analysts at MMS International.
The federal funds rate opened at 5-13/16 percent, near the current target level of 5.25 percent.
-- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663
